matters.title: To authorize the additional purchase of replacement portable radio parts with EarPhone Connection using funds from the 2022 SPLOST program, Radio Equipment Replacement, Program B1020.
matters.text:
On November 3, 2020, voters approved the 2022 Special Purpose Local Option Sales Tax (2022 SPLOST), which provides for capital improvements, including radio equipment replacement as an eligible item under 2022 SPLOST, Tier 1, 4.4 Radio Equipment Replacement, with a budget of $16 million.
During the deployment phase of the new radio equipment, the manufacturer discontinued the current remote speaker microphone and the connecting cable for the earpiece due to supply chain shortages. New remote speaker microphones are being procured separately, but they require a different connecting jack. A compatible jack is available through the vendor EarPhone Connection. This purchase will allow the 800MHz unit to replace the discontinued earpiece cable with one that is compatible with the new microphones which remain available from the original manufacturer.
In accordance with the Policy on Procurement and Contract Management, as amended by the Board on January 14, 2020, three written quotes are typically required for purchases over $2,000.00. However, only one vendor, EarPhone Connection, was identified as the sole manufacturer of this item. A Sole Source Request was approved by Support Services for this purchase on September 12, 2024.
Funding for the purchase is available in the 2022 SPLOST Fund 348-130-B102-B1020. This agenda item has been reviewed by County Finance and aligns with the Public Safety Strategic Outcome Area.

matters.title: To approve a five-year sole source Master Services Agreement (MSA) with Pictometry International Corp. (Pictometry) for cloud software, acquisition of updated digital aerial imagery, planimetric data collection, LiDAR and contours to be integrated into the Cobb County Geographic Information System (GIS).
matters.text:
Since 2004, Pictometry International Corp. has provided Cobb County with a library of digital aerial imagery and the software required to store and view these images. The Pictometry GIS image library allows users to view and analyze any house, building, intersection, fire hydrant, tree, or other feature in the County from their computers and mobile devices.
On October 24, 2017, the Board of Commissioners approved a three-year agreement with Pictometry to provide updated digital aerial imagery and software for the County’s GIS for FY 18 - FY 20. This agreement, dated June 13, 2018, resulted in flyovers #1 - #3.
On October 27, 2020, the Board of Commissioners approved a three-year renewal and Amendment #1 to the agreement with Pictometry to provide updated digital aerial imagery and software for the County’s GIS for FY 2021 - FY 2023. The agreement resulted in flyovers #4 - #6.
On March 8, 2022, the Board of Commissioners authorized additional collection for impervious data to add planimetric updates to the County’s GIS. The Department informed the Board that a periodic collection schedule would be developed to keep the data up to date. The next planimetric capture will be in 2025, which is year two of the five-year contract.
On July 25, 2023, the Board of Commissioners authorized the addition of gravel surfaces to the impervious surface data collection in the County’s GIS. This addition will continue to be included in the planimetric capture in 2025. 
The Department requests approval of a five (5) year MSA with Pictometry for cloud software, annual flyovers to acquire updated digital aerial imagery, planimetric data collection in year two, and LiDAR and contours in year three. The MSA shall be one (1) year with annual automatic renewals for a maximum four (4) renewals.
The cost of the five-year MSA is an amount not to exceed $1,569,259.70. This MSA has been reviewed by the County Attorney’s Office. Funding details are as follows:

matters.title: To approve the relocation and restoration of the Power-Jackson Cabin at Hyde Farm, under the 2011 PARKS SPLOST Program, and further approve Leatherwood, Inc as the sole source vendor for the restoration services.
matters.text:
The 2011 PARKS SPLOST Program includes the restoration of historic buildings at Hyde Farm, located at 721 Hyde Road, Marietta. This project includes the restoration of the Power-Jackson Cabin which is planned to be relocated to Hyde Farm. 
PARKS, Community Development (Historic Preservation), Cobb Landmarks & Historical Society (Cobb Landmarks) and the National Park Service (NPS) have worked together to plan for the relocation of the Power-Jackson cabin to Hyde Farm. The cabin is one of the last remaining examples of a single-pen log house with a rived log construction found in Cobb County. Testing is scheduled by Cobb Landmarks to more accurately date the cabin but it is thought to possibly date before 1840. The cabin is privately-owned and threatened by prolonged neglect and site development. 
Two other Power cabins are already located at Hyde Farm. The Power-Hyde House (c.1840s) was the home of several Power siblings to farm and settle in Cobb after the forced removal of the Cherokee. This home and the surrounding farm are currently being reviewed by the NPS for listing on the National Registry of Historic Places. Just South of Hyde Farm, the George Abner Power House (c.1843) is owned by Cobb Landmarks. This home was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2001. 
In 2014, Leatherwood, Inc. restored the 13 structures on the Hyde Farm site. In order to maintain the historic integrity and continuity of the farm and follow NPS guidelines, proper restoration of the Power-Jackson cabin is essential to achieving the preservation of the cabin as well as the farm. A Sole Source request has been approved to allow Leatherwood, Inc. to perform the restoration work. 
Cobb Landmarks has raised the money necessary to disassemble and move the cabin to Hyde Farm. Cobb Landmarks is prepared to contract with Leatherwood, Inc. to perform that work. Leatherwood, Inc. has submitted a proposal to PARKS in the amount of $321,000.00 to perform the work necessary to restore the cabin once it is relocated to Hyde Farm. Procurement Services has approved the Sole Source Request, not to exceed $321,000.00.
This project aligns with the Quality of Life Strategic Outcome Area.

matters.title: To approve a sole source agreement with Georgia Fire & Rescue for the purchase of 80 new thermal image cameras.
matters.text:
Cobb County Fire and Emergency Services (CCFES) is presently in the process of upgrading its fleet of thermal imaging cameras. Under our structured 5-year replacement program aimed at keeping pace with technological advancements, we are poised to implement this transition. Furthermore, our commitment to quality assurance is underscored by a comprehensive 5-year bumper-to-bumper warranty. 
In alignment with our dedication to operational excellence, we remain steadfast in our decision to retain Bullard Imagers from Georgia Fire & Rescue, who is a sole source vendor. The decision is rooted in their proven track record of superior performance, reputable customer service, and warranty coverage.
It is crucial that the new cameras maintain identical specifications to ensure seamless integration with our existing training protocols and operational procedures. This uniformity not only optimizes efficiency but also facilitates streamlined training and maintenance processes.
CCFES is requesting the procurement of the Bullard QXT Pro thermal imaging cameras. This acquisition is intended to replace our existing camera inventory while additionally expanding our fleet with an additional 8 units.
CCFES allocates resources for the replacement of fleet cameras every five years, taking into consideration both wear and technological advancements. Thermal imaging cameras play a vital role in assisting firefighters by enabling them to detect and locate individuals in smoke-filled environments through the interpretation of thermal and heat signatures.
The Bullard QXT Pro cameras boast upgraded software algorithms and advanced image interpretation capabilities, resulting in superior image clarity and the industry's quickest image processing. Furthermore, enhancements to the display scene colorization contribute to an improved visual experience for operators.
This sole source has been reviewed and approved by the Procurement Office.
